newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill spot, repo rates end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill spot, repo rates end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Monday after Beijing launched a sudder crackdown on the stock markets, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rose to 117.87 yuan from 116.46 last Friday.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market increased sharply to 4.64 million lots from 940,293.

"Some speculative funds have flowed back to the spot market after the crackdown on the stock markets," said one trader. "But the funds need time to pull out of the stocks and the impact on the spot market will be limited in the near term.
Traders expect spot prices to go up slightly tomorrow.
Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up with some institutions borrowing money to trade on the spot market after the stock crackdown, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract advanced to 15.00 percent from 4.00 percent last Friday.
Combined turnover rose to to 8.41 million lots from 7.53 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Although the repo rates were down at midday due to the crackdown, they were carried up later by heavy buying from institutions who borrowed for spot trading," one traders said.
